claims.finding: Brady completed an acquisition on 2026-08-06 - 8-K items 1.01, 2.01, 2.03, 7.01, 9.01, i.e. a definitive agreement, completed acquisition and new indebtedness in one filing - identified in the corpus as Honeywell's Productivity Solutions and Services business, and this 2026-09-03 print is the first release and the first FY27 guide that will consolidate it; the stock has fallen from $98.24 on the day of completion to $90.18 the night before the print.

claims.why_not_priced: A first guide that consolidates a business of roughly the acquirer's own size is the single largest revision event a name like this gets, and the tape moved the wrong way for it: -8.2% between deal completion and the print on rising volume, with the 20-day run-up negative. If the market had marked the deal to a new earnings base it would not be trading below where it closed the transaction. There is no sell-side preview anywhere in this capture (n_queries=0 in every sweep) to show whether published FY27 estimates include the acquired business at all - and when they do not, the first guide is a step-change.
claims.independence: Two separate pre-print corpus items from different Stocktwits participants on 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-02 independently frame the print the same way - 'their forward looking statements will be more valuable than actual earnings numbers' - which is a second, non-EDGAR pointer at the same guidance-reset asymmetry: docs/9da54838be70866b1935a4bc20f1299650419c48.txt

claims.finding: Volume on 2026-09-02, the session immediately before this before-the-open print, was 454,000 shares against a 185,865 twenty-day average - 2.4x normal and the single largest day in the whole captured price series - while the stock closed at the low of its three-week range at $90.18.

claims.why_not_priced: A 2.4x volume day before a bmo print with nothing in the news corpus to explain it is a positioning fact that no aggregator publishes. Note the caveat: four Form 4s were filed the same day and Brady's fiscal year ends 31 July, so at least part of that activity is likely routine annual equity grants and settlement rather than a directional build - which is why I size this small and wide.
